# Commit history

Every commit on `main`, newest first, numbered as GitHub counts them (the first commit is 1). Each shows the pull request it merged, the branch commits that pull request squashed into it, the files it changed and the rest of its message. The pull requests closed without merging come last.

- **Through:** commit 610, [`79274be`](https://github.com/aryamahadik/rosie/commit/79274be), 2026-11-14 09:58:47 UTC.
- **Merges:** `main` has 0 merge commits. Every pull request is squash-merged into one commit, after QA, its reviews and one green merge-check.
- **Updates:** the build regenerates this file after each merge (`scratch/build/lead/commit-history.mjs`). Each update is itself a commit, so it appears in the next update.

K-21 v1 signInCheck and signOut in actions/src/page-calls/sign-in over K-05 v1.13 proveSignIn and endSession (the Tool API's client) and personStanding and signInEntries (the runtime side's client): hand-written K-21 request checks held to Ajv; the device's sha256, the typed code's keyed hash (a null code as no digits) and a session drawn for every check (a 32-byte token, of which K-05 gets the sha256, and a 128-bit id); K-05's answers mapped to K-21's labels alone (never the code's id, the attempt's server id or the session's), the standing read after signedIn, tester only on staging, a failed read failing closed; secondProofNeeded with both of K-21's ways; the entries after the answer under the attempt's id or the sign-out's request id, none for an attempt with no code; labels-only spans. - **Pull request:** [#562](https://github.com/aryamahadik/rosie/pull/562) from `task/T-1348`, merged 2026-11-13 13:24:21 UTC. It squashed 1 branch commit:
  - `442e9a5` T-1348: a danger whose pending note was never written is read again u…
- **Files changed:** 2 (+451 −26), by folder:
  - `runtime/src/safety/` arrival.ts +100 −20, hold.worker.test.ts +351 −6

<details><summary>The commit message below its subject line</summary>

~~~text
waiting() names a text whose danger flag is set and whose hold is not written, its note or not, and the
danger's first application sets its re-read 30 s on, so a replay or an outbox path whose hold write threw
is tried again on the read's own schedule. resumeCutOff treats a cut-off text whose flag is set as a
danger in application and writes its missing note; applyLate does the same when such a danger's re-read
answers. applyLate, keepLabels and onReturn read dangerOpen (the note, or the flag with the hold not
written or the result owed), so a later No never clears the flag or replaces the labels or kept result.
onlyHoldLeft takes the flag in place of a missing note. The line, the at-once release, sendDanger and
sendOutage are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
~~~

</details>

* T-1108: the batch and joined-turn spans, one receive span per event with sealedToActor and firstTrace, and one count of places (seq) across a trace's writers; the draft checked against the card and K-08 and reworked

trace: a trace id's writers in one isolate share one count (beginSeq, resumeSeq, takeSeq, TraceContext.shareSeq and reserve); a hop takes its place as it starts; toTrace reads by seq; closeBatch takes a place per text and leaves an id that is no label out of the span. gateway (Linq and email doors): the one receive span says sealedToActor, a repeat's names firstTrace as the actor's door answers it; the door's places are taken before the hand-off and told to the actor (seqBefore); a shared count opens only once the signature has passed. actor: no receive span of its own; the count is kept in storage as its sinks write, never lowered, and brought back only for traces still in flight; the batch window takes the batch spans' places before the pin and writes them after it (the turn's under the pinned bundle id, a joined text's under its own), once per turn id, a restart's from the close that restarted it.

tests: K-08's shape in runtime/test/trace-e2e (GAPS keeps clockHops, clockTurnId, clockJobId, receiptTrace), new unit and worker tests beside the code, the actor, hop2, pin and lease-turn tests moved from the closed gaps' old shape to K-08's, and tests/e2e/skeleton's three closed gaps taken off (one narrower gap, modelCallOrder, stays named).

  - `b06c689` T-1153: deploy-preview.sh refuses a branch whose diff holds a path wi…

<details><summary>The commit message below its subject line</summary>

~~~text
* T-1153: deploy-preview.sh builds the Tool API's validators in the worktree after npm ci and before the upload

node runs the worktree's own infra/build/tool-api-validators.mjs (infra/ is guarded), never an npm script
of the branch's; a failed build stops the preview before anything is migrated or uploaded. GUARDED_PATHS
adds **/node_modules and **/node_modules/**: the generated code imports Ajv's run-time helpers by package
name, so a node_modules a branch commits would otherwise run during the build's self-check. Tests: the build
after npm ci and before the upload, a failing build with no upload, and the three new refusals.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-1153: deploy-preview.sh's guarded paths ignore letter case, and a symbolic link in a branch's diff is refused (DL-453 round 2)

Every GUARDED_PATHS entry is now :(glob,icase), since this Mac's volume ignores case: a branch's Node_Modules, PACKAGE.JSON or .NPMRC is refused as node_modules, package.json and .npmrc are. Step 0 also refuses any entry of the branch's git diff --raw with mode 120000 on either side, so a link (say at actions/src/tool-api/generated) cannot point the build's writes or its cleanup outside the worktree; the lead can still preview a reviewed link with PREVIEW_ALLOW_INFRA=1, and its notice lists each path once. Tests: refusals for Node_Modules, PACKAGE.JSON and .NPMRC; a link where the build writes and one of main's files made a link, each named as a link; a link named node_modules named as both; a reviewed link previewed. The 20 earlier tests are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-1153: deploy-preview.sh refuses a branch whose diff holds a path with a byte outside printable ASCII (DL-456 round 3)

git's icase folds ASCII letters only, but this Mac's volume also folds U+017F to s and U+212A to k, so a node_modules or package.json spelt with them passed step 0. Step 0 now pipes git diff --no-renames --raw -z <base> <sha> into node, which reads it NUL-separated and byte by byte and lists every path, on either side of an entry, that holds a byte outside 0x20-0x7E. Such a branch is refused under its own 'paths with characters outside printable ASCII' line, each path quoted as git quotes paths whatever core.quotePath says; PREVIEW_ALLOW_INFRA=1 lifts it after review, as for guarded files and links, and the notice lists each path once. Output that git diff --raw -z should never give stops the script. main holds no such path (git ls-files -z and git ls-tree -r -z main: 3502 paths). Tests: refusals for generated/node_module(U+017F)/ajv/dist/runtime/equal.js, generated/pac(U+212A)age.json, an accented name, a tab and a newline in one name, DEL and a removed path; a guarded accented path named in both lists and previewed once reviewed; a space and a tilde previewed; the quoting with core.quotePath off. The 27 earlier tests are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
~~~

</details>

<details><summary>The commit message below its subject line</summary>

~~~text
* T-1198: the actor's readCommit learns of safety timers from the commit's core results, not from written alone

Since T-1194 (actions/src/commit default 9; K-09 v1.5 default 134), K-09's written leaves every core action's rows out. readCommit now also counts a core result that went through (no error, a response) whose call is not one of K-09's 15 core actions, none of which writes a K-34 safety_timers row: a later core action that writes a timer reloads the actor's timer copies. A refused core action wrote nothing; a repeat's core results count, as it answers its first commit. Today's commits read as before.

Tests: a core action writes Sam's timer that written leaves out and the actor still reloads and copies it (moved, then safe); readCommit on a later core action's result (refused, repeated, malformed); each of K-09 v1's core actions, read from the frozen schema, reads nothing. The Tool API double takes timersByCore and keeps its answers.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-1198: round 2 (DL-413): readCommit fails safe, and a repeat reloads the timer copies (T-1203 folded in)

A core result that is not K-09's coreResult now reloads the actor's safety-timer copies instead of reading no: not a record, no string call, no error field, an error that is not K-09's refusal (a JSON object with its own error code), or error null with a response that is not a record. A refused result still reads no. An answer in K-09's shape (written a record) reloads when its core results are missing or not a list, its repeated is not false, or its rows are not a list; a row that names no table reloads too. A repeat (K-09 repeated true) reloads, since its first answer, maybe lost, named the rows and the repeat answers with written []. A first answer keeps rules 1 and 2. A null answer and written in neither shape read as before.

Tests: the malformed-shape assertion now expects the reload, for each of 16 shapes one at a time; K-09-shaped answers that cannot be read; repeats against first answers (each of K-09's 15 core calls, stop-recorded.json repeated); the actor test where the first commit writes Sam's timer row, its answer is lost and the repeat answers with written []: the copy reloads and holds the row; a repeat with no timer reloads and the copy stays as it was. The Tool API double gains loseNextAnswer, and the timer rig sends a lost answer's request again once, as turn.ts sendWithResend does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ProposedPrice is a union by basis: a list price always has its amount; only a photo quote (null until priced) or a price set at the visit or by the hour may have none. readProposal reads the price once (readPrice): a photo quote not priced yet waits (notPricedYet, A4-05), an at-visit or hourly price passes noted minimumNotChecked, and a list price with no amount or a basis none of the sources names throws, so neither limit 2 nor search (which has no limit 2 around it) ever holds it, noted or not; minimumCheck goes unchecked only for those two reads. Tests: a 250 dollar minimum with a list price of no amount (extras none, 60 or 300 dollars) and with an unknown basis (priced or not) throws, with or without rules; a photo quote with no amount still waits and at-visit and hourly prices still pass noted; at limit 2 decide and check reject and the gate's call rolls back after limits 1 and 2

<details><summary>The commit message below its subject line</summary>

~~~text
Check 3 attempt 4 had one denial: a QA agent ran git log with
backslash-escaped spaces (--format=%h\ %s\ %p). Claude Code refuses
that form in an unattended shift although git log is allowed; the
quoted form runs. CLAUDE.md now says to write one plain command per
call and to quote values with spaces. It also says the Glob and Grep
tools may be missing and to list folders with ls.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
~~~

</details>
